item: Both full-suite jobs list skips FIRST with -rsfE (the test job's -rfEs put the failing names out of a log tail's reach), and scripts/preflight.sh stops claiming the test job's EXACT commands; a test pins both
summary: Both the test and the Core-only job run python -m pytest -q -rsfE. The test job's -rfEs (from #1663) printed FAILED and ERROR BEFORE the skip block, and pytest prints the summary in the order of the letters (pytest 9.1.1: -rfEs prints FAILED, ERROR, SKIPPED; -rsfE prints SKIPPED, FAILED, ERROR), so on a red run the last lines of the log, all a tail reader gets, were skips and the names of the failing tests sat above them; -rsfE puts the failures last. Found by this PR's Opus read. scripts/preflight.sh said it ran the test job's EXACT commands: its pytest line lacks the job's flags (kept off on purpose: a bare sandbox skips hundreds of tests and that block would bury the failures the advisory run is read for), it omits most of the job's steps, and its mypy gate compared an error count to MYPY_BASELINE, which ci.yml stopped defining on 2026-08-20, so it fell back to 127 and printed PASS for 1 to 126 errors where the job goes red on one. The gate is now mypy's exit status; the header says which commands are verbatim, how the pytest line differs and what is not run, and the closing line no longer says Safe to push. tests/test_ci_pytest_flags_and_preflight.py pins the flags of both jobs and preflight's ruff and mypy CALLS (read from its executed lines, not its echo lines or comments) against ci.yml, with mutants at one site each that must be named; it fails on the unedited files and passes on the edited ones. Stated limits: the Core-only skip block was not read from a runner log (the log tail tool returns about 13 KB); preflight.sh was run end to end without --tests, its --tests branch only syntax-checked; the hundreds-of-skips figure is the 2026-10-29 audit's local count (373), not re-measured here.
